ev.q: During 2021, an estimated 20.9% of U.S. adults (51.6 million persons) experienced chronic pain
Between 2019 and 2021, the prevalence of chronic pain among U.S. adults ranged from 20.5% to 21.8%
The age-adjusted prevalence of high-impact chronic pain among AI/AN adults (12.8%) was six times as high as among non-Hispanic Asian adults (2.1%)
The age-adjusted prevalence of chronic pain among adults identifying as bisexual was 32.9%, compared with 19.3% among adults identifying as straight
NHIS is a cross-sectional, household survey of the civilian, noninstitutionalized population

methods_quotes.q: including estimated number, crude rates, and age-adjusted rates with Korn-Graubard 95% CIs
Age-adjusted rates were calculated because the prevalence of pain is reported to vary by age
All reported differences between subgroups in crude rates and in age-adjusted rates were significantly different on the basis of two-tailed Z-tests (p<0.05).
